yzoh9l:204: Progress state is written to two carriers simultaneously — a highly scannable terminal summary for humans (numbers, ratios, anomalies) and a structured state file for the Agent to read (task ID, state, artifact path, failure reason). The deep logic of this design: humans need an intuitive sense of "how far it's gotten" when resuming; the Agent needs precise instructions on "where to continue from". The two data structures are completely heterogeneous. Forcibly merging them not only creates redundancy, but also increases parsing noise for the Agent. Many teams implement persistence but overlook the dual-channel design — a common hidden cause of long-running task recovery failures.
